title: Rename the about_me field to bio

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "The profile field `about_me` is now called `bio` in the API.". The schema change adds data_key='bio' to about_me field, making the API accept 'bio' instead of 'about_me' in PUT /api/me requests, causing validation error for 'about_me' field.

suspicions.claim: The API now returns 'bio' instead of 'about_me' in user profile responses, breaking clients expecting the old field name.
suspicions.trigger: Log in via POST /api/tokens with basic auth (e.g., alice:doppel-pass), save access_token, then GET /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Read the JSON response and verify the profile field is named 'bio' (new) instead of 'about_me' (old).
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/me returned about_me in base and bio in head for alice (f5, f21) and carol (f9).

suspicions.claim: Clients sending 'about_me' in PUT /api/me to update their profile will have the value ignored because the schema only loads 'bio'.
suspicions.trigger: Log in as alice, then PUT /api/me with JSON {'about_me': 'new bio text'} and Authorization: Bearer <token>. Read the response JSON and observe that the returned profile field (now 'bio') still has the old value, confirming the input was ignored.
suspicions.evidence: PUT /api/me with about_me returned 200 with about_me in base but 400 with unknown field error in head (bob_probe).

suspicions.claim: Clients must now send 'bio' in PUT /api/me to update the profile; sending 'about_me' no longer works.
suspicions.trigger: Log in as alice, then PUT /api/me with JSON {'bio': 'updated bio'} and Authorization: Bearer <token>. Read the response JSON and verify the 'bio' field reflects the new value.
suspicions.evidence: PUT /api/me with bio returned 400 with unknown field error in base but 200 with bio updated in head (carol_probe).

suspicions.claim: User registration (POST /api/users) now requires 'bio' instead of 'about_me'; sending 'about_me' will be ignored or cause validation errors.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON {'username': 'newuser', 'email': 'new@example.com', 'password': 'pass', 'about_me': 'ignored'}. Read the response: if status 201, check that the returned user object has 'bio' field (likely null/empty) and not 'about_me'. Then repeat with 'bio': 'hello' and verify it appears in the response.
suspicions.evidence: POST /api/users with about_me returned 201 in base but 400 with unknown field error in head; with bio returned 400 in base but 201 with bio in head (dave_probe).

suspicions.claim: Public user profiles (GET /api/users/<id> and GET /api/users/<username>) now return 'bio' instead of 'about_me'.
suspicions.trigger: GET /api/users/1 (or /api/users/alice) with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Read the JSON response and verify the profile field is named 'bio'.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/1 returned about_me in base and bio in head (f22, erin_probe); GET /api/users/carol returned about_me in base and bio in head (f8, f18).

suspicions.claim: Paginated user collections (e.g., followers, following) now include 'bio' instead of 'about_me' in each user object.
suspicions.trigger: GET /api/users/1/followers with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Read the JSON response and inspect the first item in 'data' array: it should have a 'bio' field and no 'about_me' field.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/1/followers returned about_me in base and bio in head (f6, f23, frank_probe); GET /api/me/following returned about_me in base and bio in head (f7).
